title: Maximus: The Hundred Worlds - Courier Manual

pages.head: The Light Went Out
pages.html:
Maximus: The Hundred Worlds

Sector Zero, the year the stars went quiet.

For ten thousand years the Maximus Core burned at the heart of the galaxy: a forge-star whose light ran down the warp lanes to every inhabited world. Couriers rode that light from planet to planet, carrying everything from seed grain to love letters.

Then the Core cracked. Its light was held in ten star-shards, and when it broke they were flung across the Hundred Worlds. The warp lanes are failing. Sector by sector, the galaxy is going quiet.

Max is a courier at Maxima Station. Couriers deliver. This time the package is the light of the galaxy: find the ten shards, carry them through the gates, fly the Maelstrom, and bring them home to the Heart.

pages.head: Getting Started
pages.html:
Installing

Copy every file on the disk into one directory, for example C:\MAXIMUS, and type MAXIMUS. You need a 386 or better with VGA and 640K. A Sound Blaster plays the music and the digitized effects; without one, the PC speaker plays them.

The menu

  • Play starts at Maxima Station's training deck.
  • Read Instructions, Read Storyline and See Credits show the pages from this manual on screen.
  • Leave the menu alone for half a minute and Max shows you around the training deck himself.

The training deck

The deck teaches as you go: walk, hop the crates, pick up credits, shoot the practice drones, pay the credit door, ride the lift and walk into the airlock. Then you are in the pod.

Lives and saving

You start with 3 lives and 100 hit points. Lose them all and the signal is lost. Save often with F5: it is a big galaxy.

pages.head: Four Ways to Travel
pages.html:
The courier pod

Space charts are flown in the pod. The arrows fire its thrusters; let go and it brakes. Fly into the middle of a planet to land, into a warp ring to jump.

On foot

Max's suit has grav-jets: Up is a hop, and another tap in the air hops again. Hold Right while you tap Up to sail over gaps. Walk into the uplink beacon behind you to return to orbit.

The diving bell

On sea worlds Max takes the bell. It swims with the arrows and coasts when you let go. Bubble columns lift you, currents push you. Surface at the buoy to leave.

The rover

Rover worlds are fast and flat. The rover rides the lifts at every step; with the Spring Shocks module it can jump.

pages.head: The Galaxy and the Shards
pages.html:
Sector gates

The galaxy chart holds five sector warps around the dead Core. The Cradle is open; every other sector is sealed by crystal gates, two to a sector. A gate opens when you touch it carrying its shard, and the shards stay with you for good.

SectorGate needsWorlds
1. The Cradleopen18
2. EmberreachRuby + Amber18
3. The ShallowsCitrine + Emerald18
4. GlasswindJade + Aqua18
5. The Deep BlackSapphire + Amethyst16
The Coreall ten3

Jump rings

Every sector chart also holds a jump ring, walled in behind the next sector's crystal gates: carry those shards and it takes you straight on. The ring in The Deep Black leads to the Maelstrom itself.

Finding shards

Planets with a gold signal beside them on the sector chart hold a shard, deep in a vault. The planet card you see on landing names the shard, and the long-range scan after it shows the whole world: where you land (green) and where the vault lies (gold).

Trading posts

Each chart has a trading post. Nudge a pad to buy: an extra life (100 credits), repairs (20), plasma cells (30), nova charges (40), shield charges (30) and med kits (50). One of each per visit.

pages.head: Worlds and Vaults
pages.html:
What you will find

  • Credits (green chips), gems (score), hearts (hit points), 1-Ups and ammo cells for your modules.
  • Vaults deep underground hold the shards and modules. A credit door costs 10 credits to open; a force field blinks on and off.
  • Crystal walls shatter at a touch, and some rock is not rock at all: secret pockets hide treasure.
  • Lifts and bubble columns carry you up; winds and currents push you along.
  • Lava, acid and brine hurt, but the jolt hops you out. Healing springs mend you.
  • Nests in cave walls send out creatures until you leave.

pages.head: Courier Modules
pages.html:
The ten modules

Modules lie in planet vaults. Press P to pick one up; it stays in your inventory (F2) and works in every vehicle that can use it.

Ammunition counts carry from vehicle to vehicle. The Plasma Lance is the only weapon that cracks armor; the Shield Emitter's guard orb stops almost anything.

pages.head: Creatures
pages.html:
On the worlds

GloopA hopping slime. Harmless alone, never alone.
Gloop MotherSplits into a Gloopling when shot.
GlooplingSmall, fast, and it follows you.
ShellbackA beetle walking its beat.
IronbackArmored. Blaster bolts bounce off; use the Plasma Lance.
DropwebHangs from cave ceilings and drops on you.
FlitterA cave bat with no sense of direction.
ScreechA bigger bat that dives when you come near.
StingerWasps home in on courier suits.

In the seas

MinnowSmall fry darting about in schools.
SnapfinA toothy little fish that comes straight for you.
BigfinCruises back and forth along the reef.
AnglerWaits in the dark, then lunges at your lamp.
Ribbon EelSwims long laps through open water.
MorayLurks in holes and snaps at passers-by.

In space

Void JellyDrifts between the stars.
Void MiteTiny, fast and drawn to engines.
Pirate SkiffFlies a patrol line.
Pirate AceHunts couriers for their cargo.
RaiderFlies figure eights around its loot.
Scout DroneWanders and watches.

On the stations

CrawlerA maintenance bot gone bad.
Sentry DroneWanders the corridors.
Gun TurretBolted to the deck. Armored.
Security BotArmored patroller.
Spider BotDrops from the ceiling.
Hover MineBobs in place.

Most creatures burst when they hit you. A few things - flytraps, magma, tumbling asteroids, the Phantom - cannot be hurt at all: keep moving.

pages.head: Registering Maximus
pages.html:
This is shareware

Copy it, share it, upload it. If you enjoy Maximus, please register: registration is $15 and gets you the printed manual with a fold-out galaxy chart, the courier's sector map of all 88 worlds and their vaults, the hint book, and news of our next game.

Credits

Designed and built by Claude for Sandbox Software, with Game-Maker 3.0 by Recreational Software Designs. Every world, sprite, song and sound was made by a program from a seed.

pages.head: Pushing the Limits
pages.html:
How far Game-Maker goes

Maximus was built to stand on every edge of Game-Maker 3.0. These are the limits we found in its file formats and in PLAYGAME, and how much of each this game uses (also in LIMITS.TXT on the disk).

LimitMaximumMaximus uses
Scenes in a .GAM231 (PLAYGAME allocates all scenes in one 64K block of 283-byte records)100: title, ending, training deck, galaxy, 5 sectors, 88 worlds, Maelstrom, Citadel, Heart. We stopped at 100: 28300 bytes of scene records sit easily in DOS memory, every scene still loads in a moment, and the integrator's 310x165 world view still shows each scene box and link
